Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 73, verse 1–4:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿O you who are wrapped up (in garments)﴾ (1) ﴿Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little﴾ (2) ﴿Half of it, or lessen it a little﴾ (3) ﴿Or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾ (4)

By His words ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ is meant the one wrapped in his garments. He meant by this none other than the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ).

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning in which Allah described His Prophet (ﷺ) with "al-muzzammil" (the one wrapped up) in this verse. Some of them said: He described him as one wrapped in his garments, prepared for prayer.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, meaning the one wrapped in his garments.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ is the one who wrapped himself in his garments.

Others said: He described him as one wrapped in prophethood and messengership.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His words: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little﴾, he said: "You have been wrapped in this matter, so rise to it."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of this is what Qatadah said, because He followed it with His words: ﴿Stand through the night﴾. So this was an explanation that his description as "wrapped" refers to garments for prayer, and that this is the more apparent of its two meanings.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little﴾

He says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Stand through the night﴾, O Muhammad, all of it, ﴿except a little﴾ of it, ﴿half of it﴾, meaning: stand half the night, ﴿or lessen it a little, or add to it﴾, meaning: or add to it. Allah, the One mentioned, gave him the choice when He made the night prayer obligatory upon him, among these stages, to do whichever he wished. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions, it is related, used to stand through the night, similar to their standing in the month of Ramadan, until this was lightened for them.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, who said: Sammak al-Hanafi narrated to us, who said: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When the beginning of al-Muzzammil was revealed, they used to stand in prayer roughly like their standing in Ramadan, and between its beginning and its end was close to a year.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Mis'ar, who said: Sammak narrated to us, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say, and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "roughly like their standing in the month of Ramadan."

Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Hayyan narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, who said: Muhammad ibn Tahla', client of Umm Salamah, narrated to me, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to make a reed mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to pray upon during the night. The people heard of it and gathered, and he came out as one who was angry, and he was merciful to them. He feared that the night prayer would be prescribed for them, so he said: "O people, take upon yourselves of deeds what you are able to do, for Allah does not tire of rewarding until you tire of working, and the best of deeds is that which you persist in." And the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿O you who are wrapped up, stand through the night, except a little, half of it, or lessen it a little, or add to it﴾, until a man would tie a rope and hold on to it. They persisted in this for eight months, and Allah saw what they sought of His good pleasure, so He had mercy on them, returned them to the obligation, and abandoned the night prayer.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah al-Himyari, from Muhammad ibn Tahla', from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'A'ishah, who said: I used to buy a reed mat for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he would stand upon it from the beginning of the night, and the people heard of his prayer, and a group of people gathered. When he saw their gathering he disliked it, and feared that it would be prescribed for them, so he entered the house as one who was angry. They began clearing their throats and coughing until he came out to them and said: "O people, indeed Allah does not tire until you tire" — meaning in reward — "so take upon yourselves of deeds what you are able to do, for the best of deeds is the most constant of them, even if it is little." And there was revealed to him: (O you who are wrapped up, stand through the night, except a little) the surah. She said: So it was prescribed for them, and it came down in the status of an obligation, until one of them would tie a rope and hang on to it. When Allah saw what they were burdened with, which they sought by it the face of Allah and His good pleasure, He lifted it from them, and said: ﴿Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾ ... up to ﴿He knew that you would not be able to keep count of it, so He turned to you (in forgiveness)﴾. So He returned them to the obligation and lifted the supererogatory prayer from them, except what they did voluntarily.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿Stand through the night, except a little, half of it, or lessen it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾: Allah commanded His Prophet and the believers to stand through the night, except a little, and that was difficult for the believers. Then He lightened it for them and had mercy on them. And after this Allah revealed: ﴿He knows that there will be among you those who are sick, and others who travel through the land﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾. So Allah widened the matter, and to Him be praise, and did not constrain it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: When Allah revealed to His Prophet: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, the Prophet (ﷺ) remained in this state for ten years, standing through the night as Allah had commanded him, and a group of his Companions stood with him. Then Allah revealed to him, after ten years: ﴿Indeed your Lord knows that you stand (in prayer) nearly two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it, and a group of those with you﴾ ... up to His words: ﴿And establish prayer﴾. So Allah lightened it for them after ten years.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan, both of whom said: In Surat al-Muzzammil, ﴿Stand through the night, except a little, half of it, or lessen it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾ was abrogated by the verse in which is: ﴿He knows that you will not be able to keep count of it, so He turned to you (in forgiveness). So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾.

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Stand through the night, except a little﴾: They stood for a year or two years until their shins and feet swelled, so Allah revealed a later lightening at the end of the surah.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Wahb, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: When ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ was revealed, they stood in prayer with it for a year, until their feet and shins swelled, until there was revealed: ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾, and the people were relieved.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jarir, seller of cloaks, from al-Hasan, who said: "Praise be to Allah," supererogation after an obligation.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: When ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾ ... the verse was revealed, the Muslims stood for a year, some of them were able to bear it and some were not, until the concession was revealed.

He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Sammak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the beginning of al-Muzzammil was revealed, they used to stand in prayer roughly like their standing in the month of Ramadan, and between its beginning and its end was roughly a year.

As for His words: ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾

He, may He be exalted and glorified, says: Clarify the Qur'an when you recite it, clarifying it, and recite it slowly and deliberately.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have spoken in accordance with what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said this:

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words: ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: Recite it with a clear recitation.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: one part following upon another.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: one part following upon another, deliberately.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: Recite it slowly and deliberately.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: one part following upon another.

Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, from 'Ata', concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: tartil is nabdh, meaning casting aside.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: make it clear with clarity.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: make it clear with clarity.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And recite the Qur'an with measured recitation﴾, he said: one part following upon another.

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning in which Allah described His Prophet (ﷺ) with "al-muzzammil" (the one wrapped up) in this verse. Some of them said: He described him as one wrapped in his garments, prepared for prayer.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿O you who are wrapped up﴾, meaning the one wrapped in his garments.

The Tafsir of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 73, verses 5–7:

Regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾: some of the people of interpretation said that it means: "Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word," meaning acting upon it.

Those who said this:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾, he said: "Acting upon it. A man may recite the surah quickly [[al-hadh: speed of recitation. One says "yahudhdhu al-Qur'an hadhdhan" when he recites it quickly and continuously. This narration is cited in al-Taj.]], but acting upon it is heavy."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿a heavy word﴾: "Heavy, by Allah, are its obligations and its limits."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿heavy﴾: "Heavy, by Allah, are its obligations and its limits."

Others said: Rather, it means that the word itself is heavy in what it carries.

Those who said this:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that "when the Prophet ﷺ received revelation while on his she-camel, she would lower her chest (jiran) to the ground, and she could not move until it was lifted from him."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's words, ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾: "By Allah, it is heavy and blessed. Just as it was heavy in this world, it will be heavy in the scales on the Day of Resurrection."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is that it should be said: Allah described it as a heavy word, so it is as He described it: heavy in what it carries, and heavy in acting upon its limits and obligations.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, the rising at night (nashi'at al-layl), it is firmer in tread﴾:

By His words ﴿the rising at night﴾, the Exalted and Mighty means: the hours of the night, and every hour of the night is a "rising" of the night.

The people of interpretation differed regarding this.

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah informed us, saying: I said to 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah: "Will you not tell me which part of the night is the nashi'ah?" He said: "You have fallen on the right one. I asked Ibn 'Abbas about it, and he claimed that the whole night is nashi'ah. I asked Ibn al-Zubayr about it, and he told me the same."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: 'Anbasah related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "In the language of Abyssinia, when a man stands up in the night, they say: nasha'a (he rose)."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿the rising at night﴾: "Nasha'a: stood up."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Maysarah, regarding ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "Nasha'a: stood up."

- He said: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, who said: "When a man stands up in the night, that is the rising of the night."

- Hannad ibn al-Sari related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "It is the whole night."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "If you stand in prayer at night, that is the rising."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "Everything after the 'isha' prayer is the rising."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾: "It is the night prayer (qiyam al-layl). He said: At whatever hour of the night one stands up, he has risen."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "At whatever part of the night you stand, that is the rising."

- He said: Mihran related to us, from Kharijah, from Abu Yunus Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, who said: "I asked Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr about the rising of the night, and both said: 'The whole night is the rising. When you rise up standing, that is the rising.'"

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "At whatever hour one of the worshippers (mutahajjid) performs night prayer."

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾: "It means the whole night."

- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz and Nafi', from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "The whole night."

- He said: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The whole night: when one stands to pray, that is the rising."

Others said: Rather, it refers to what occurs after the 'isha' prayer, and what occurs before the 'isha' is not nashi'ah.

Those who said this:

- He said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Abu Raja' related to us, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "What comes after the final 'isha' prayer."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾, he said: "The rising at night is what comes after the 'isha' prayer."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Sulayman related to us, saying: Abu Hilal related to us, who said: Qatadah said, regarding His words, ﴿the rising at night﴾: "Everything after the 'isha' prayer is the rising."

As for His words: ﴿it is firmer in tread (ashaddu wat'an)﴾:

The reciters of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) differed in reciting this. The majority of the reciters of Makkah, Madinah and Kufa recited ﴿ashaddu wat'an﴾ with a fatha on the waw and a sukun on the ta'. Some reciters of Basra, Makkah and Syria recited ﴿wiṭa'﴾ with a kasrah on the waw and a long alif, as a verbal noun (masdar) from the saying of the speaker: "wati'a al-lisan al-qalb mu'atha'atan wa wiṭa'" (the tongue agreed with the heart in agreement and accord).

The Tafsir of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 73, verses 5–7:

Regarding the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾: some of the people of interpretation said that it means: "Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word," meaning acting upon it.

Those who said this:

- Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, We will cast upon you a heavy word﴾, he said: "Acting upon it. A man may recite the surah quickly [[al-hadh: speed of recitation. One says "yahudhdhu al-Qur'an hadhdhan" when he recites it quickly and continuously. This narration is cited in al-Taj.]], but acting upon it is heavy."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿a heavy word﴾: "Heavy, by Allah, are its obligations and its limits."

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿heavy﴾: "Heavy, by Allah, are its obligations and its limits."

Others said: Rather, it means that the word itself is heavy in what it carries.

Those who said this:

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that "when the Prophet ﷺ received revelation while on his she-camel, she would lower her chest (jiran) to the ground, and she could not move until it was lifted from him."

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is that it should be said: Allah described it as a heavy word, so it is as He described it: heavy in what it carries, and heavy in acting upon its limits and obligations.

The reciters of the major cities (qurra' al-amsar) differed in reciting this. The correct view regarding this, in our opinion, is that both are well-known recitations and both are sound in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter recites is correct.

By His words ﴿it is firmer in tread﴾ is meant: the rising at night is firmer and more stable than the day, and more firmly fixed in the heart, because acting at night is more lasting than acting by day. Those among the people of interpretation who recited it with a fatha on the waw and a sukun on the ta' said something similar to what we have said, although their expressions differ.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 73, verses 8–10:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And remember the name of your Lord and devote yourself to Him with complete devotion (tabtil)﴾

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And remember﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿the name of your Lord﴾, so call upon Him by it. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ means: and detach yourself toward Him, detaching (from all else) for your needs and your worship, apart from all other things besides Him. It derives from the expression "tabattaltu hadha al-amr" (I devoted myself to this matter). From this comes the designation of the mother of Jesus, son of Mary, as al-Batul (the chaste, the one devoted), because of her detachment toward God. It is also said of a worshipper who detaches himself from the world and its causes toward the worship of God: "qad tabattal" (he has devoted himself). From this is the report transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that "he forbade tabattul" (the monastic detachment from marriage and worldly life).

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the east and the west﴾

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it with the nominative (raf'), as a new beginning, since it is a complete verse after another. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the genitive (khafd), as an adjective (na't) and as a referent to the pronoun in His saying: ﴿and devote yourself to Him﴾.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are well-known readings, and scholars among the reciters have read each of them, so whichever reading the reader uses is correct. The meaning of the speech: Lord of the east and the west and what lies between them of the creation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿There is no god but He﴾

He says: it is not fitting that any god be worshipped other than God, who is the Lord of the east and the west.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿so take Him as Disposer of affairs (wakil)﴾

In what He commands you, and entrust your affairs to Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And be patient over what they say and part from them with gracious parting﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): be patient, O Muhammad, over what the polytheists of your people say to you, and over their harm, and part from them for God's sake with gracious parting. The gracious parting (hajr jamil) is the parting for the sake of God, as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than it﴾ ... the verse. It was also said that this was abrogated.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And be patient over what they say and part from them with gracious parting﴾: "Bara'a (Surat al-Tawba) abrogated what is here; He commanded fighting them until they bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and nothing else from them is accepted."

Al-mahil is a passive participle from the saying of the speaker: "hallat al-raml, fa-ana uhayluhu" (I poured out the sand, so I pour it), which is when the bottom of it is stirred and it collapses from above onto it. The Arabs have two forms for this: they say mahil and mahyul, and makil and makyul. Among that is the poet's saying:

Your people used to consider you a lord, and I think you are a lord who has been struck by the evil eye (maghyun).

He said: The passive participle from this pattern came sound, thereby differing from the active participle, because the passive participle does not follow its verb in its vowels and quiescence as active participles follow their verbs; the passive participle differed from its verb in its inflection, as we have mentioned.]

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: burdened by it.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: laden and burdened.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: it will be burdened by that Day.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: This is the Day of Resurrection, so He made the young grey-haired, and the Day the sky is split, and he recited: ﴿When the sky splits asunder﴾ and said: All of this is the Day of Resurrection.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abdullah ibn Yahya, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: filled with it, in the language of Abyssinia.

Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, but he did not hear it from Ibn Abbas: ﴿The sky will be split by it﴾: He said: filled with it.

The sky is mentioned in this place because the Arabs use it both as masculine and feminine. Whoever uses it as masculine directs it to the ceiling, as one says: "this is the sky of the house," meaning its roof. It may also be that they make it masculine because it is among the nouns in which there is no distinction between feminine and masculine forms. Of the masculine usage is the saying of the poet:

"Had He raised the sky up to Him with a people, we would have joined the sky along with the clouds."

[[The verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 346), where he said: His saying "the sky will be split by it" refers to that Day. The sky is used both as masculine and feminine, so here it is in the masculine form; the poet said: "Had He raised the sky..." the verse. Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 181): "The sky will be split by it": Abu Amr said: he dropped the ta' marbuta, because its meaning is the ceiling; one says "this is the sky of the house." Some said: the Arabs sometimes drop the feminine markers from feminine nouns, being content without them; one says "mahra damir" and "imra'a talaq," and the meaning is "munfatirah."]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿His promise is ever fulfilled﴾

Your Lord, the Exalted, says: what God promised to do is certain to be done, because He does not break His promise; and what He promised to bring about, by His command, is that the Day when children become grey-haired will occur. He says: therefore beware of that Day, O people, for it is certain to come.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it, and [so do] a group of those with you. And Allah determines the night and the day. He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it, so He has turned to you in forgiveness. So recite what is easy from the Qur'an. He knows that there will be among you those who are ill, others traveling throughout the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy from it and establish prayer and give zakah and loan Allah a goodly loan. And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (73:20)

He, exalted is His mention, says by His saying: Indeed, these verses in which He mentioned the matter of the Resurrection and its terrors, and what He will do therein to the people of disbelief, are a reminder (tadhkirah), meaning: a lesson and an admonition for whoever takes heed from them and is warned. ﴿So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾ means: whoever among the creation wills may take to his Lord a path by believing in Him and acting in obedience to Him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, this is a reminder﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿so whoever wills may take to his Lord a way﴾ by obedience to Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] almost two thirds of the night or half of it or a third of it﴾

He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, knows that you stand in prayer closer to two thirds of the night, and half of it, and a third of it.

The reciters differed in reading this: The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it with the genitive (khafd), "and half of it and a third of it" meaning: "and [you stand] for less than half of it and a third of it" — that you could not bear to perform what was enjoined upon you of night prayer, so stand for close to two thirds of the night and for half of it and a third of it. And some of the reciters of Mecca and the majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the accusative (nasb), meaning: you stand for close to two thirds of the night and you stand for half of it and a third of it.

The correct view regarding this is that both are well-known readings, sound in meaning; whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. His saying: ﴿and a group of those with you﴾ means: from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who were believers in Allah when night prayer was enjoined upon them.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah determines the night and the day﴾

By hours and times.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾

He says: Your Lord has known, O people upon whom night prayer was enjoined, that you will not be able to sustain its standing, ﴿so He has turned to you in forgiveness﴾ when you were unable and weak to do it, and He returned to you with lightening for you.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said similarly to what we have said regarding the meaning of His saying: ﴿that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan: ﴿He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾, that you will not be able to bear it.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn Rashid informed me of it, saying: I heard al-Hasan say regarding His saying: ﴿that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾, he said: You will not be able to bear it.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id: (He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it) he says: that you will not be able to bear it.

He said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan: ﴿He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾, he said: that you will not be able to bear it.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two qualities, no Muslim man counts them except that they admit him to Paradise. They are easy, but those who act upon them are few: he glorifies Allah (tasbih) ten times after every prayer, praises Him ten times, and magnifies Him ten times." He said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting them on his hand. He said: "That is one hundred and fifty on the tongue, and one thousand five hundred on the scale. And when he goes to his bed, he glorifies, praises, and magnifies Him a hundred times; that is a hundred on the tongue and a thousand on the scale. So which of you does two thousand five hundred evil deeds in a single day?" They said: "Then how would we not count them?" He said: "Satan comes to one of you while he is in his prayer and says: Remember such-and-such, remember such-and-such, until he turns away, and perhaps he does not understand. And he comes to him while he is in his bed and keeps putting him to sleep until he sleeps."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿He has known that you will not be able to keep count of it﴾: the night prayer was prescribed upon you. ﴿So recite what is easy from the Qur'an﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So recite what is easy from the Qur'an﴾

He says: So recite from the night what is easy for you of the Qur'an in your prayer; and this is a lightening from Allah, mighty and majestic, upon His servants of the obligation He had imposed upon them by His saying: ﴿Stand [to pray] the night, except for a little - half of it - or subtract from it a little﴾.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja' Muhammad, who said: I said to al-Hasan: O Abu Sa'id, what do you say about a man who has memorized the entire Qur'an by heart, yet does not stand (in night prayer) with it, but only performs the obligatory prayer? He said: He takes the Qur'an as a pillow; may Allah curse that one. Allah said to the righteous servant: ﴿And indeed, he is one of knowledge because of what We taught him﴾ and ﴿You have been taught what you did not know, you nor your fathers﴾. I said: O Abu Sa'id, Allah said: ﴿So recite what is easy from the Qur'an﴾. He said: Yes, even fifty verses.

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from 'Ushman al-Hamdani, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿So recite what is easy from the Qur'an﴾, he said: a hundred verses.

He said: Waki' narrated to us, from Rabi', from al-Hasan, who said: Whoever recites a hundred verses in a night, the Qur'an will not argue against him.

He said: Waki' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ka'b, who said: Whoever recites a hundred verses in a night is recorded among the worshippers.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He has known that there will be among you those who are ill, and others traveling throughout the land seeking of Allah's bounty﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Your Lord has known, O believers, that there will be among you people of illness whom illness has weakened from standing in night prayer, ﴿and others traveling throughout the land﴾ on a journey, ﴿seeking of Allah's bounty﴾ through trade, who have traveled to seek livelihood and it disabled them, weakening them also from standing in night prayer. ﴿And others fighting in the cause of Allah﴾ means: and others also among you strive against the enemy, fighting them in support of the religion of Allah. So Allah had mercy on you and lightened [the obligation] for you, and removed from you the obligation of standing in night prayer. ﴿So recite what is easy from it﴾ means: so recite now, since that has been lightened for you, from the night in your prayer, what is easy of the Qur'an. The pronoun in His saying "from it" refers to the mention of the Qur'an.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said similarly to what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Then He informed about the qualities of the believers, saying: ﴿He has known that there will be among you those who are ill, and others traveling throughout the land seeking of Allah's bounty, and others fighting in the cause of Allah. So recite what is easy from it﴾. He said: Allah had made standing (in night prayer) obligatory at the beginning of this surah, so the Prophet of Allah ﷺ and his companions stood for a year until their feet swelled, and Allah held back its conclusion for twelve months in the heavens; then He sent down the lightening at its end, and the night prayer became a voluntary act after an obligation.

﴿And establish prayer﴾ means: and establish the prescribed prayer, which is the five prayers in the day and night. ﴿And give zakah﴾ means: and give the prescribed zakah from your wealth to its people.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said similarly to what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And establish prayer and give zakah﴾: they are two obligatory duties, with no concession for anyone regarding them, so discharge them to Allah, exalted is His mention.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And loan Allah a goodly loan﴾

He says: And spend in the cause of Allah from your wealth.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And loan Allah a goodly loan﴾: the loan is the voluntary charities other than zakah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whatever good you put forward for yourselves - you will find it with Allah, better and greater in reward﴾

He says: And whatever you, O believers, send forward for yourselves in the life of this world of charity or spending you spend in the cause of Allah, or other spending in ways of good, or deed of obedience to Allah such as prayer, fasting, or pilgrimage, or other deeds of good seeking what is with Allah — you will find it with Allah on the Day of Resurrection in your return; it will be better for you than what you sent forward in this world, and greater in reward: that is, its reward is greater than that which you sent forward, had you not sent it forward. ﴿And seek forgiveness of Allah﴾ means, exalted is His mention: and ask Allah to forgive your sins, that He may pardon you for them. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: indeed, Allah is possessor of forgiveness for the sins of whoever of His servants repents of his sins, and possessor of mercy in not punishing them for them after their repentance from them.

End of the interpretation of Surah al-Muzzammil.
